#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

typedef struct Node {
    int key;
    int height;
    struct Node *left;
    struct Node *right;
} Node;

/* Maximum of two numbers */
int max(int a, int b) {
    return (a > b) ? a : b;
}

/* Height of node */
int height(Node *node) {
    if (node == NULL)
        return 0;

    return node->height;
}

/* Create a new node */
Node *createNode(int key) {
    Node *newNode = (Node *)malloc(sizeof(Node));

    newNode->key = key;
    newNode->height = 1;
    newNode->left = NULL;
    newNode->right = NULL;

    return newNode;
}

/* Right rotation */
Node *rightRotate(Node *y) {
    Node *x = y->left;
    Node *t2 = x->right;

    x->right = y;
    y->left = t2;

    y->height = 1 + max(height(y->left), height(y->right));

    x->height = 1 + max(height(x->left), height(x->right));

    return x;
}

/* Left rotation */
Node *leftRotate(Node *x) {
    Node *y = x->right;
    Node *t2 = y->left;

    y->left = x;
    x->right = t2;

    x->height = 1 + max(height(x->left), height(x->right));
    y->height = 1 + max(height(y->left), height(y->right));

    return y;
}

/* Balance factor */
int getBalance(Node *node) {
    if (node == NULL)
        return 0;

    return height(node->left) - height(node->right);
}

/* Insert into AVL tree */
Node *insert(Node *root, int key) {

    if (root == NULL)
        return createNode(key);

    if (key < root->key) {
        root->left = insert(root->left, key);
    }
    else if (key > root->key) {
        root->right = insert(root->right, key);
    }
    else {
        /* Duplicate element */
        return root;
    }

    root->height =
        1 + max(height(root->left), height(root->right));

    int balance = getBalance(root);

    if (balance > 1 && key < root->left->key)

        return leftRotate(root);

    /* LR Case */
    if (balance > 1 && key > root->left->key) {

    if (balance < -1 && key < root->right->key) {
        root->right = rightRotate(root->right);
        return leftRotate(root);
    }

    return root;
}

/* Find minimum node */
Node *minValueNode(Node *root) {
    Node *current = root;

    while (current != NULL && current->left != NULL)
        current = current->left;

    return current;
}

/* Delete from AVL tree */
Node *deleteNode(Node *root, int key) {

    if (root == NULL)
        return NULL;

    if (key < root->key) {
        root->left = deleteNode(root->left, key);
    }
    else if (key > root->key) {
        root->right = deleteNode(root->right, key);
    }
    else {

        /* No child */
        if (root->left == NULL && root->right == NULL) {
            free(root);

        /* Only right child */
        if (root->left == NULL) {
            Node *temp = root->right;
            free(root);

        }

        if (root->right == NULL) {
            Node *temp = root->left;
            free(root);

        }

        Node *temp = minValueNode(root->right);

        root->key = temp->key;

    }

S.No: 2 Exp. Name: Operation of B-Tree - Insertion, Deletion and Search Date: 2026-08-11
Aim:

Write a C program to construct a B-Tree of a given minimum degree. First, insert a list of keys into the B-Tree and print the inorder traversal after all insertions. Then, delete a given set of keys from the B-Tree and again print the inorder traversal. Finally, search for a specific key in the current B-Tree and print whether it is found or not.


Input Format:

  • The first line contains a single integer t, the minimum degree of the B-Tree.
  • The second line contains an integer n, representing the number of keys to be inserted.
  • The third line contains n space-separated integers — the keys to be inserted into the B-Tree.
  • The fourth line contains an integer d, the number of keys to delete.
  • The fifth line contains d space-separated integers — the keys to be deleted from the B-Tree.
  • The sixth line contains a single integer k — the key to be searched in the B-Tree.


Output Format:

  • The first line of output should display the inorder traversal of the B-Tree after all insertions, with each key separated by a space.
  • The second line should display the inorder traversal of the B-Tree after all deletions, with each key separated by a space.
  • The third line should print Found if the search key exists in the B-Tree. If the key is not present, print Not Found instead.



Note: Refer to the test cases for better understanding.

typedef struct BTreeNode {

// Create a new node
BTreeNode* createNode(int t, bool leaf) {
BTreeNode* node = (BTreeNode*)malloc(sizeof(BTreeNode));
node->t = t;
node->leaf = leaf;
node->keys = (int*)malloc((2 * t - 1) * sizeof(int));
node->C = (BTreeNode**)malloc((2 * t) * sizeof(BTreeNode*));
node->n = 0;
return node;
}
// Inorder traversal (no trailing dot)
void inorder(BTreeNode* root) {
if (!root) return;

void heapifyUp(int i){
	while(i > 0 && heap[(i-1) / 2] > heap[i]) {
		swap(&heap[i], &heap[(i-1) / 2]);
		i = (i-1) / 2;

}

void swap(int*a,int*b){

void heapifyUp(int index){
	while(index>0 && heap[(index-1)/2]<heap[index]){
		swap(&heap[index],&heap[(index-1)/2]);
		index=(index-1)/2;
	}
}
void insert(int value){
	heap[size]=value;
	heapifyUp(size);
	size++;
}
void heapifyDown(int index){
	int largest=index;
	int left=2*index+1;
	int right=2*index+2;
	if(left<size && heap[left]>heap[largest])
		largest =left;
	if(right<size && heap[right]>heap[largest])
		largest =right;
	if(largest!=index){
		swap(&heap[index],&heap[largest]);
		heapifyDown(largest);
	}
}
void deleteMax(){
	if(size==0)

	heap[0]=heap[size-1];
	size--;
	heapifyDown(0);
}

#include<stdio.h>
#include<stdlib.h>
#define MAXV 1000
#define MAXE 2000
int graph[MAXV][MAXV];
int disc[MAXV],low[MAXV];
int time = 0;
int bccCount =0;
int edgeStack[MAXE];
int stackTop=-1;
void dfs(int u,int parent,int n){
	disc[u]=low[u] = ++time;
	for(int v=0;v<n;v++){
		if(!graph[u][v])
			continue;
		if(v==parent)
			continue;
		if(disc[v]==0){
			edgeStack[++stackTop]=u*MAXV+v;
			dfs(v,u,n);
			if(low[v]<low[u])
				low[u]=low[v];
			if(low[v]>=disc[u]){
				while(stackTop >=0){
					int edge=edgeStack[stackTop--];
					int x=edge/MAXV;
					int y=edge%MAXV;
					if(x==u && y==v)
						break;
					if(x==v && y==u)
						break;
				}
				bccCount++;
			}
		}
		else if(disc[v]<disc[u]){
			edgeStack[++stackTop]=u*MAXV +v;
			if(disc[v]<low[u])
				low[u]=disc[v];
		}
	}
}

	int n,e;

void quicksort(int a[],int lb,int ub);
int partition(int a[],int lb,int ub);
void swap(int *p1,int *p2);
int main(){
	int n;
	scanf("%d",&n);
	int a[n];
	for(int i=0;i<n;i++)
		scanf("%d",&a[i]);
	quicksort(a,0,n-1);
	for(int i=0;i<n;i++)
		printf("%d ",a[i]);
	printf("\n");
	return 0;
}
void quicksort(int a[],int lb,int ub){
	if(lb <ub){
		int pos = partition(a,lb,ub);
		quicksort(a,lb,pos -1);
		quicksort(a,pos +1,ub);
	}
}
int partition(int a[],int lb,int ub){
	int left=lb;
	int right =ub;
	int pivot =a[lb];
	while(left<right){
		while(left<=ub && a[left]<=pivot){
			left++;
		}
		while(a[right]>pivot){
			right--;
		}
		if(left<right){
			swap(&a[left],&a[right]);
		}
	}
	swap(&a[lb],&a[right]);
	return right;
}
void swap(int*p1,int *p2){
	int temp;
	temp =*p1;

#include <stdio.h>
void merge(int a[],int lb,int mid,int ub){
	int i=lb;
	int j=mid+1;
	int k=lb;
	int b[100];
	while(i<=mid && j<=ub){
		if(a[i]<=a[j]){
			b[k]=a[i];
			i++;
		}else{
			b[k]=a[j];
			j++;
		}
		k++;
	}
	while(i<=mid){
		b[k]=a[i];
		i++;
		k++;
	}
	while(j<=ub){
		b[k]=a[j];
		j++;
		k++;
	}
	for(i=lb;i<=ub;i++){
		a[i]=b[i];
	}
}
void mergeSort(int a[],int lb,int ub){
	if(lb<ub){
		int mid =(lb+ub)/2;
		mergeSort(a,lb,mid);
		mergeSort(a,mid+1,ub);
		merge(a,lb,mid,ub);
	}
}

S.No: 13 Exp. Name: Job Sequencing using Greedy Problem Date: 2026-09-22
Aim:

Given a set ofNjobs, where eachjob ihas a deadline and a profit associated with it. Each job takes1unit of time to complete, and only one job can be scheduled at a time. We earn the profit associated with the job if and only if the job is completed by its deadline. Find the number of jobs done and themaximum profit.


Note:Jobs will be given in the form (Job Id, Deadline, Profit) associated with that Job. The deadline of the job is the time by which the job needs to be completed to earn the profit.


Input Format:

  • The first line contains an integer N representing the number of jobs.
  • The next N lines each contain three space-separated integers: {Job ID, Job Deadline, Job Profit} — representing one job per line.


Output Format

  • Two integers separated by a space:
  • The first integer represents the number of jobs done.The second integer represents the maximum profit obtained.


Constraints:

  • 1≤N≤105
  • 1≤Deadline≤N
  • 1≤Profit≤500


Example 1:

Input: 

4
1 4 20 
2 1 10 
3 1 40 
4 1 30

Output: 

2 60

Explanation: Job 1and Job 3 can be done with a maximum profit of 60 (20+40).


Note: Refer to the test cases for better understanding.

JsGreedy.c
#include<stdio.h>
#define MAX 100
int main(){
	int n;
	scanf("%d",&n);
	int id[MAX],deadline[MAX],profit[MAX];
	int i,j;
	for(i=0;i<n;i++){
		scanf("%d %d %d",&id[i],&deadline[i],&profit[i]);
	}
	for(i=0;i<n-1;i++){
		for(j=i+1;j<n;j++){
			if(profit[i]<profit[j]){
				int temp;
				temp=profit[i];
				profit[i]=profit[j];
				profit[j]=temp;
				temp=deadline[i];
				deadline[i]=deadline[j];
				deadline[j]=temp;
				temp=id[i];
				id[i]=id[j];
				id[j]=temp;
			}
		}
	}

	int slot[MAX]={0};
	int jobDone=0,maxprofit=0;
	for(i=0;i<n;i++){
		for(j=deadline[i];j>0;j--){
			if(slot[j]==0){
				slot[j]=1;
				jobDone++;
				maxprofit=maxprofit+profit[i];
				break;
			}
		}
	}
	printf("%d %d\n",jobDone,maxprofit);
	return 0;
}

S.No: 14 Exp. Name: Program to implement Knapsack problem Using Dynamic Programming Date: 2026-10-06
Aim:

You are given n items, each with a specific weight and value. You have a knapsack with a maximum capacity W. Your goal is to select a subset of these items such that the total weight is less than or equal to W, and the total value is as large as possible.


This is the classic 0/1 Knapsack problem, where each item can either be included once or excluded from the knapsack.


Input Format:

  • The first line contains an integer n, representing the number of items to consider for the knapsack.
  • The second line contains n space-separated integers, representing the weights of the items.
  • The third line contains n space-separated integers, representing the values of the items, corresponding to their weights.
  • The fourth line contains an integer W, representing the capacity of the knapsack.


Output Format:

  • Print the maximum profit that can be obtained by selecting items such that their combined weight does not exceed the knapsack capacity.


Note: Refer to the test cases for better understanding.

dynamicKs.c
#include <stdio.h>
int main(){
	int n,i,capacity;
	scanf("%d",&n);
	int weigths[n];
	int values[n];
	for(i=0;i<n;i++){
		scanf("%d",&weigths[i]);
	}
	for(i=0;i<n;i++){
		scanf("%d",&values[i]);
	}
	scanf("%d",&capacity);
	int dp[capacity+1];
	for(i=0;i<=capacity;i++){
		dp[i]=0;
	}
	for(i=0;i<n;i++){
		for(int w=capacity;w>=weigths[i];w--){
			if(dp[w-weigths[i]] +values[i]>dp[w]){
				dp[w]=dp[w-weigths[i]]+values[i];
			}
		}
	}
	printf("%d\n",dp[capacity]);
	return 0;
}

Aim:

Write a C program to solve the N-Queens problem using backtracking. The goal is to place N queens on an N×N chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. A queen can attack another queen if they share the same row, column, or diagonal. Your program should print the first valid configuration of the board found by placing queens from left to right and top to bottom, using a backtracking approach. The board must be displayed as an N×N matrix where a cell contains 1 if a queen is placed there, and 0 otherwise. If no solution exists for the given value of N, print a message indicating that no solution exists.


Input Format:

  • A single integer N — the number of queens and the size of the chessboard.


Output Format:

  • If a solution exists, print an N×N matrix consisting of 0s and 1s, where 1 represents a queen.
  • If no solution exists, print: "No solution exists for N = <value>".
  • Each row of the matrix should be printed on a new line, with space-separated values.


Note: Refer to the test cases for better understanding.

nqueens.c
#include<stdio.h>
#include<stdbool.h>
#define MAX 20
int board[MAX][MAX];
void printSolution(int n){
	for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
		for(int j=0;j<n;j++){
			printf("%d ",board[i][j]);
		}
		printf("\n");
	}
}
bool isSafe(int row,int col,int n){
	int i,j;
	for(i=0;i<row;i++){
		if(board[i][col]==1) return false;
	}
	for(i=row,j=col;i>=0 && j>=0;i--,j--){
		if(board[i][j]==1) return false;
	}
	for(i=row,j=col;i>=0 && j<n;i--,j++){
		if(board[i][j]==1) return false;
	}
	return true;
}
bool solveNQueens(int row,int n){
	if(row==n){
		return true;
	}
	int col;
	for(col=0;col<n;col++){
		if(isSafe(row,col,n)){
			board[row][col]=1;
			if(solveNQueens(row+1,n)){
				return true;
			}
			board[row][col]=0;
		}
	}
	return false;
}
int main(){
	int n;
	scanf("%d",&n);

		return 0;
	}
	int i,j;
	for(i=0;i<n;i++)
		for(j=0;j<n;j++)
			board[i][j]=0;
	if(solveNQueens(0,n)){
		printSolution(n);
	}else{
		printf("No solution exists for N = %d\n",n);
	}

}

  • The next n lines each contain two space-separated integers: the value and weight of an item.
  • The last line contains an integer W, representing the capacity of the knapsack.

knapsackBacktracking.c
#include<stdio.h>
int n;
int w;
int maxProfit=0;
int values[100],weights[100];
void knapsack(int i,int currentWeight,int currentValue){
	if(i==n){
		if(currentValue >maxProfit)
			maxProfit =currentValue;
		return;
	}
	if(currentWeight +weights[i]<=w){
		knapsack(i+1,currentWeight+weights[i],currentValue+values[i]);
	}
	knapsack(i+1,currentWeight,currentValue);
}
int main(){
	scanf("%d",&n);
	for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
		scanf("%d %d",&values[i],&weights[i]);
	}
	scanf("%d",&w);
	knapsack(0,0,0);
	printf("%d\n",maxProfit);
	return 0;
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <limits.h>
int n;
int cost[20][20];
int visited[20];
int minCost=INT_MAX;
void tsp(int city,int count,int currentCost,int start){
	if(count ==n){
		if(cost[city][start]!=-1 && currentCost+cost[city][start]<minCost){
			minCost =currentCost+cost[city][start];
		}
		return;
	}
	for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
		if(!visited[i]&& cost[city][i]!=-1){
			visited[i]=1;
			tsp(i,count+1,currentCost+cost[city][i],start);
			visited[i]=0;
		}
	}
}
int main(){
	scanf("%d",&n);
	for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
		for(int j=0;j<n;j++){
			scanf("%d",&cost[i][j]);
		}
	}
	for(int i=0;i<n;i++){
		visited[i]=0;
		visited[0]=1;
		tsp(0,1,0,0);
		printf("%d\n",minCost);
		return 0;
	}
}
